dialogue.content: すみません、部屋間違えしておりました。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry, I had the wrong room.

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: おはようございます。大変申し訳ありません。よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. My sincere apologies. Thank you for your understanding.

dialogue.content: おはようございます、今日はよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. Thank you for meeting with me today.

dialogue.content: snsカウンセリングを始めさせて頂きます。本日はどのような相談内容になりますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Let's begin our online counseling session. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 今日はママ友の事でお話を聞いていただきたいのですが
dialogue.English: Today, I'd like to talk about an issue with a mom friend.

dialogue.content: はい。どう言った内容になりますか？
dialogue.English: Yes. What kind of issue is it?

dialogue.content: 幼稚園に通う娘がおり、娘の友達の母親と仲がよかったのに、最近私を避けるようになりました。
dialogue.English: I have a daughter in kindergarten, and I was good friends with her friend's mother, but lately she's started avoiding me.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。それは、どうして？となりますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. That would make you wonder, "Why?"

dialogue.content: はい。娘同士のトラブルが原因で、それまでは仲が良かったのに。
dialogue.English: Yes. It's because of some trouble between our daughters. We were good friends before that.

dialogue.content: 元々、
dialogue.English: You see,

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ちょっと疑問があると、直ぐに悪口を言うタイプのママ友で
dialogue.English: she's the type of mom-friend who immediately starts bad-mouthing people if she has the slightest issue.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 娘が、友達を避けるようになったんですね。しつこく遊びに誘ってくるみたいで
dialogue.English: My daughter started avoiding her friend. It seems the friend was being too persistent about asking her to play.

dialogue.content: それで、
dialogue.English: And so,

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 少し距離おきたいみたいで、仲間はずれにしたことがあるんです
dialogue.English: it seems she wanted to keep a bit of distance, so there was an instance where she left her out.

dialogue.content: そこは娘には話をし注意をしたのですが、
dialogue.English: I talked to my daughter about it and told her not to do that, but...

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 娘は他の子と遊びたいのに、しつこくされて余計に距離を取りたい。それで、その友達が仲間に外れにすると
dialogue.English: My daughter wants to play with other kids, but the friend is so persistent that it makes her want even more distance. And when she excludes her friend,

dialogue.content: 母親に言うみたいで、
dialogue.English: she apparently tells her mother,

dialogue.content: 数回メールでやり取りしたのですが、
dialogue.English: I exchanged a few emails with the other mom, but...

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 納得いかないみたいで、そこから、避けるようなりました。
dialogue.English: she doesn't seem to be satisfied, and from that point on, she started avoiding me.

dialogue.content: なるほど、これはなかなかモヤモヤする内容ですよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. That sounds like a very frustrating situation.

dialogue.content: そうなんです
dialogue.English: Yes, exactly.

dialogue.content: 先生とも話をして、
dialogue.English: I also spoke with the teacher,

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: まぁ、この年齢の子供同士の関係ではあることだし、お互い悪い所があるので、特に2人はしばらく見守ってくれるという話になり、
dialogue.English: and we agreed that these things happen between children this age, that both have their faults, so they'll just keep an eye on the two of them for a while.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: おまかせしたんです。もちろん自分も
dialogue.English: so I left it in their hands. Of course, I also—

dialogue.content: なるほど。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 娘と話しますが、やはり、その場で考えて解決しないといけないと思うんです
dialogue.English: I talk to my daughter, but I feel they need to learn to think and resolve these things themselves in the moment.

dialogue.content: でも、ママ友は納得いかないみたいで、
dialogue.English: But the other mom doesn't seem to agree,

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: この前迎えに行った時、娘に直接
dialogue.English: The other day at pick-up, she directly said to my daughter—

dialogue.content: 「なんでそんなことするの？」って、突然言ったみたいで
dialogue.English: 'Why would you do something like that?' she apparently said, all of a sudden.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 娘も突然言われて、キョトンですよね
dialogue.English: My daughter was suddenly confronted and was just baffled.

dialogue.content: そうなりますよね。
dialogue.English: That’s understandable.

dialogue.content: そして、ママ友の娘ちゃんにも距離をおきなさいと言ってみたいなのですが
dialogue.English: And it seems she also told her own daughter to keep her distance from mine.

dialogue.content: その娘ちゃんはうちの娘と遊びたいし
dialogue.English: But her daughter wants to play with my daughter,

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: とても悪循環なんです。
dialogue.English: It's a really vicious cycle.

dialogue.content: なるほど、確かに悪循環ですよね。
dialogue.English: I see, it certainly does sound like a vicious cycle.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: こちらの思いは伝えているし、なんなら、1度ご飯でもたべながら話す？って伝えたのですが、拒否してくるし
dialogue.English: I’ve shared my perspective, and I even asked if she'd like to talk it over a meal sometime, but she refused.

dialogue.content: なるほど。
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: どうにも動けなくて、、
dialogue.English: I feel stuck and unable to move forward…

dialogue.content: どうしたらいいでしょうか
dialogue.English: What should I do?

dialogue.content: 良い状態に戻して行きたいですよね。少し整理して行きましょうか。
dialogue.English: You'd like to get things back to a good place, right? Shall we try to organize our thoughts a bit?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: この問題が発生したのはいつぐらい前からですか？
dialogue.English: About how long ago did this problem start?

dialogue.content: トラブルがあることを知ったのは3ヶ月くらい前です
dialogue.English: I found out about the trouble about three months ago.

dialogue.content: それ以前からもあった言われたのですが、どの程度かは不明です
dialogue.English: I was told it had been happening even before that, but I’m not sure to what extent.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。ママ友に避けられたなと感じたのもその辺りからですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Is that also around the time you started to feel that the other mom was avoiding you?

dialogue.content: ある日突然メールがきたんです。こういう状態だからと。その時はまだ注意してもらえると嬉しいみたいな感じでした
dialogue.English: One day, I suddenly got an email from her explaining the situation. At that time, it was more like she'd appreciate it if I could talk to my daughter about it.

dialogue.content: そこで初めて知ったので、まずは嫌な気持ちにさせてしまってごめんねと謝り、娘にも話をするねで、終わりました
dialogue.English: That was the first I'd heard of it, so I started by apologizing for making her daughter feel bad and said I would talk to my own daughter. That was the end of it.

dialogue.content: あと、先生にも伝え、見てもらうよういいました
dialogue.English: I also told the teacher and asked them to keep an eye on things.

dialogue.content: なるほど、対応としては何も問題ように思えますね。
dialogue.English: I see. Your response seems perfectly reasonable.

dialogue.content: 問題無いよう
dialogue.English: It seems fine.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: やはり、お互いその場で考えてさせないといけないので、先生に任せた方がいいと思ったんです。
dialogue.English: I really think they need to learn to think for themselves in these situations, so I thought it was best to leave it to the teacher.

dialogue.content: 向こうが納得が行かないようとありましたが、
dialogue.English: You mentioned that she doesn't seem to be satisfied...

dialogue.content: そうですよね。先生という中立な立場から見てもらうのはいいことですよね。
dialogue.English: Right. Having a neutral party like the teacher observe is a good approach.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ちなみに向こうが「納得がいかないよう」とありましたが、どの辺が納得いっていないとか、思い当たる節はありますか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned she doesn't seem satisfied. Do you have any idea what part she might be unhappy with?

dialogue.content: その後も数回、友達はどんな感じかメールしたんです。
dialogue.English: After that, I emailed her a few more times to ask how her daughter was doing.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: でも、やっぱり遊んでもらえかなった、嫌いなら嫌いでいいから、気分で遊ぼうとかやめて欲しいと。
dialogue.English: But she said her daughter still wasn't being played with, and that if my daughter dislikes her, that's fine, but she wants her to stop playing with her only when she feels like it.

dialogue.content: だから、うちの娘ともなるべく遊ばないよう伝えたと。
dialogue.English: So, she told her daughter not to play with mine if she can help it.

dialogue.content: なるほど。。
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: この人、子供のこと、全然わかってないなぁと思いました
dialogue.English: I thought to myself, "This person really doesn't understand children at all."

dialogue.content: もちろんそれは言いませんでしたが、
dialogue.English: Of course, I didn't say that to her, but...

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 嫌な気持ちにしてる事はやはり、謝り、でも、
dialogue.English: I did apologize again for hurting her daughter's feelings, but still,

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 子供自信が考えないといけないってメールしたんです
dialogue.English: I emailed her back saying that the children need to think for themselves.

dialogue.content: 先生にも言いました。
dialogue.English: I told the teacher that as well.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: でも、ママ友は、娘が可哀想みたいな感じで、、、
dialogue.English: But the other mom is just like, "My poor daughter..."

dialogue.content: なるほど。どうしても、ママ友は、親の介入という感じになってしまうのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So no matter what, the other mom insists on parental intervention.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お子様は幼稚園とのことですが、ちなみにおいくつですか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned your daughter is in kindergarten. How old is she, by the way?

dialogue.content: 5歳です
dialogue.English: She's five.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。では、あと２年くらい幼稚園に通われる感じですかね？
dialogue.English: I see. So she has about two more years of kindergarten left?

dialogue.content: 今年で最後です。ちなみに小学校も同じです
dialogue.English: This is her last year. By the way, they'll be going to the same elementary school.

dialogue.content: なるほど。少しお子様同士についてお話させてください。
dialogue.English: I see. May I ask a little about the relationship between the children?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: 男の子女の子どちらでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Are they boys or girls?

dialogue.content: 女の子です。友達も女の子です
dialogue.English: They're girls. Her friend is a girl, too.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。ママ友のお子様も女の子なのですね。
dialogue.English: Thank you. So the other mom's child is also a girl.

dialogue.content: そうです。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: 女の子はいろいろありますよね、、
dialogue.English: Things can get complicated with girls, can't they...

dialogue.content: そうですねよ、難しいですよね。。。
dialogue.English: Yes, it can be difficult...

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: お子様通しが遊び出すようになったきっかけを教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me how the children started playing together?

dialogue.content: 娘たちは入園してからずっと同じクラスで、ママ友とも仲良くて、たまにご飯を食べたりすることもあったんです。
dialogue.English: Our daughters have been in the same class since they started kindergarten, and the other mom and I were close, too. We'd sometimes go out for meals.

dialogue.content: ママ友の悩みを聞いたりすることもありました。
dialogue.English: I would sometimes listen to her concerns.

dialogue.content: だいたい愚痴とかですか、
dialogue.English: Mostly venting and complaints.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 家族同士の付き合いから仲良くなられたんですね。
dialogue.English: So you became close through family interactions.

dialogue.content: ですので、娘たちも幼稚園以外で遊ぶことがあり、仲はいいんです
dialogue.English: Yes, so our daughters would also play together outside of kindergarten, and they get along well.

dialogue.content: なるほど。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: そして、愚痴は多い方だったんですね。
dialogue.English: And she tended to complain a lot.

dialogue.content: ですが、友達が、娘を好きすぎて(？)、たまにしつこく来るのが娘は嫌みたいで
dialogue.English: However, her friend likes my daughter so much (?), that she's sometimes too persistent, which my daughter seems to dislike.

dialogue.content: うんうん。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: ちょっと苦手意識もでてきてる感じですかね
dialogue.English: I guess you could say she's starting to feel a bit wary of her.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。しつこさは、好きすぎてから来ていた可能性もあるのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So it's possible the persistence was coming from a place of liking her so much.

dialogue.content: あると思います。
dialogue.English: I think so.

dialogue.content: 娘はマイペースな方なので、どんどん来られると引いてしまう感じですね
dialogue.English: My daughter does things at her own pace, so when someone comes on too strong, she tends to withdraw.

dialogue.content: ただ、別の友達とあっちいこって言ったりすることもあるみたいです。
dialogue.English: But apparently, she sometimes says to another friend, 'Let's go over there.'

dialogue.content: うんうん。ペースを乱される感じなんですかね。
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm. It feels like her pace is being disrupted, perhaps.

dialogue.content: それは娘にも話をしています
dialogue.English: I've talked to my daughter about that.

dialogue.content: はい。朝準備をしている時にずっと引っ付いてくる感じです
dialogue.English: Yes. For example, in the morning while getting ready, the friend is clinging to her the whole time.

dialogue.content: それは娘にも話をしています。→そうしたら、お子様はどのように聞いてますか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned you've talked to your daughter about that—how does she take it?

dialogue.content: ダメなことは理解してます。でも、○○ちゃんの言うことだけきいてたら、私は楽しくないと言います
dialogue.English: She understands it's not the right thing to do. But she says, "If I only do what she wants, it's not fun for me."

dialogue.content: 意思がはっきりしているんですね。
dialogue.English: She's very clear about what she wants, isn't she?

dialogue.content: やりたいことや趣向が少し方向性が違うから、楽しく無いのかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: Perhaps it's not fun because their interests and what they want to do are a bit different.

dialogue.content: マイペースで、自分の意見はしっかりもっています。
dialogue.English: She does things at her own pace and has her own clear opinions.

dialogue.content: それもあると思います
dialogue.English: I think that's part of it.

dialogue.content: このくらいの年齢でも、あう、あわないはあると思います
dialogue.English: Even at this age, I think there are people you get along with and people you don't.

dialogue.content: うんうん。意見を持つことはとても、良いことですよね。言ってしまえば、「あわない」ということですよね。
dialogue.English: Mm-hm. Having her own opinions is a very good thing. Put simply, they may just 'not be a good fit'.

dialogue.content: だと思います
dialogue.English: I think so.

dialogue.content: ママ友というのは、お子様同士が遊んでいないとなかなか、付き合いづらい感じですかね？（仲が悪いと付き合いづらいのはあると思うのですが）
dialogue.English: With mom friends, is it hard to keep up the relationship when the children aren't playing together? (I imagine it can be harder when the kids aren't getting along.)

dialogue.content: トラブルなんてこれからたくさんあるし、私は普通にご飯食べたりも出来るのですが、向こうがあからさまに避けるんですよね
dialogue.English: There will be plenty of troubles like this in the future, and I could still go out for a meal with her like normal, but she's the one who's blatantly avoiding me.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、普通はその感覚で問題無いですよね。
dialogue.English: That's right. Normally, that way of thinking would be perfectly fine.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 避けるなら避けるでもいいのですが、悪口とかもし言われてたら嫌だなと思うことはあります
dialogue.English: If she wants to avoid me, that's fine, but I do worry that she might be bad-mouthing me.

dialogue.content: なるほど。そうですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. That makes sense.

dialogue.content: 娘同士の関係をを自分たちにリンクさせるのは違うという気持ちになりますよね。
dialogue.English: It must feel wrong for her to link her relationship with you to the one between your daughters.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ただ、向こうとしては、お子様の問題が解決しないと付き合えないというのも、やはり寂しいですよね。
dialogue.English: But from her perspective, the fact that she feels she can't be friends with you until her child's problem is resolved... that's sad, isn't it?

dialogue.content: はい。でも、子供たちが楽しくいられれば、最悪ママ友との関係はこのままでもいいかなとおもってきました。
dialogue.English: Yes. But I've started to think that as long as the children can be happy, it's okay if my relationship with the other mom stays this way, even if it's not ideal.

dialogue.content: 心の変化があるんですね。確かに、疲れちゃいますもんね。
dialogue.English: I see your feelings are changing. It's certainly exhausting, isn't it?

dialogue.content: 疲れます
dialogue.English: It's exhausting.

dialogue.content: うんうん、相談者様は、耐えているというか、頑張っていると思います。
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm, I think you've been enduring a lot, or rather, trying very hard.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 一旦まとめると仲が良かったママ友に避けられた娘同士がトラブル（幼稚園）原因はペースを乱すが故、娘が友達を避け出した（注意済み）相談者様は解決にむけて、注意や先生への報告、友達への連絡はした。ただ、話は解消に向かわない。相談者様はお子様自身のトラブルはできればお子様同士で解決させる方が良い。考えさせて解決したほうがいい。
dialogue.English: Okay, let me summarize. You were close with a mom-friend who is now avoiding you. This stems from a conflict between your daughters at kindergarten. The root cause is that your daughter feels her friend is too persistent, disrupting her pace, which led your daughter to avoid her—something you've already addressed with her. You've taken steps to resolve this, like speaking to your daughter, informing the teacher, and communicating with the other mom, but things aren't getting better. You feel that it would be best for the children to learn to resolve these issues on their own by thinking for themselves.

dialogue.content: はい、そうです
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: このまま続けていても、平行線なので、お子様同士のきっかけや友達が理解してくれるといいですよね。
dialogue.English: If things continue like this, you'll just be at a standstill. It would be great if some new opportunity arose for the children, or if the other mom could come to understand.

dialogue.content: そうなんですよね。子供たちは成長過程でいろいろ変わると思います
dialogue.English: That's true. I think children change in many ways as they grow.

dialogue.content: ただ、ママ友はどうかな、、
dialogue.English: But I'm not so sure about the other mom...

dialogue.content: 普通に話が出来るといいのですが。
dialogue.English: I wish we could just have a normal conversation.

dialogue.content: うんうん。相談者様は心の変化もあり、冷静さがあるように感じるんですよね。
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm. I feel that your perspective has shifted, and you're able to look at this calmly.

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: お友達の考えを変わるというのも時間がかかるというか、待っても変わらないですもんね。
dialogue.English: Changing your friend's way of thinking takes time—and even if you wait, it may not change.

dialogue.content: お友達の考えが
dialogue.English: Your friend's way of thinking—

dialogue.content: そうだと思います
dialogue.English: I think so too.

dialogue.content: そろそろお時間がきてしまいました。本日、相談していかがでしたか？
dialogue.English: It looks like our time is almost up. How do you feel after our discussion today?

dialogue.content: ママ友はなにかないと変わらないと思うので、とにかく子供たち自身で考えてるいけるよう、見守りたいと思います
dialogue.English: I don't think the other mom will change unless something happens, so for now, I want to watch over the children and let them learn to think for themselves.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。これから自立していく過程ですもんね。
dialogue.English: That makes sense. This is part of the process of them becoming independent.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。本日のカウンセリングを終了させて頂きます。
dialogue.English: Thank you very much. This concludes today's counseling session.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました。到らないところが多かったと思います。また、御機会ありましたらよろしくお願いします。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you. I'm sure I was lacking in many ways. I hope to have the opportunity to speak with you again.)

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、ありがとうございました！対人関係は難しいですよね、、、いろいろ学ばせていただきましたm(_ _)m
dialogue.English: Thank you as well! Relationships are so difficult... This has been a great learning experience.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます(^^)
